additional_requirements: The binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors both occur, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.

subtypes.Self-Induced Vomiting: Intentionally inducing vomiting to remove ingested food.
subtypes.Misuse of Medications: Repetitively misusing laxatives, diuretics, or enemas for the purpose of weight control.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

symptom.disease_info: Bulimia nervosa is characterized by recurrent episodes of eating unusually large amounts of food accompanied by a sense of loss of control, followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting, misuse of laxatives/diuretics, fasting, or excessive exercise to prevent weight gain. Self-evaluation is excessively and often exclusively influenced by body shape and weight, but individuals are typically within normal weight or overweight ranges, which helps distinguish bulimia from anorexia nervosa. The course is often chronic or relapsing, with symptoms waxing and waning in relation to stress, interpersonal difficulties, or changes in weight and self-esteem. It is important to differentiate bulimia from binge-eating disorder, in which compensatory behaviors are absent, and from normative overeating, which lacks the recurrent loss of control and extreme weight/shape overvaluation.

patient.personality: Gino is a meticulous, competitive retail veteran who channels his anxiety into perfectionistic attention to detail and solitary creative pursuits like painting and woodworking.
patient.stressor: Roughly seven months ago, Gino’s store brought in a much younger, fit regional manager who emphasized a “sleek, on-brand” staff image and began making comments about tightening uniforms and looking more energetic on the sales floor. Already prone to worrying over small details, Gino started fixating on how his body appeared next to his younger colleagues and how customers might judge an older, heavier salesperson in a visually focused home décor environment. In response, he began cycling between strict self-imposed food rules during the workday and episodes of eating large amounts alone at night when he felt he had failed his own standards, then resorting to increasingly desperate measures afterward to feel like he had erased the damage and could still “look the part” at work. As his preoccupation with weight and shape intensified and began to overshadow his enjoyment of art, woodworking, and even his relationship with his spouse, he sought psychiatric help at his wife’s urging after she found him distressed in the bathroom and he admitted he felt his entire value at work now hinged on how his body looked.
patient.chief_complaint: “Lately I feel like my whole sense of worth at work depends on how thin I look, and it’s gotten completely out of hand.”

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.
S046.manifestation: Ever since that new manager started going on about everyone looking 'sleek,' I can’t walk past a mirror at the store without zeroing in on my gut and love handles and thinking, ‘No one wants to buy from the old, fat guy,’ and it pretty much wipes out any pride I have in being good at my job or my art.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.
S048.manifestation: After these big eating episodes at night, I end up in the bathroom forcing myself to throw up until my throat burns, sometimes chasing it with laxatives I keep hidden in the workshop, telling myself I’m just undoing the damage so I can face the tight uniform in the morning.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: On the nights when I lose it, I’ll stand at the kitchen counter after my wife’s gone to bed and plow through leftover pasta, half a loaf of bread with butter, cookies, and whatever else is in the pantry in an hour or two—way more than any normal dinner—until I’m uncomfortably stuffed.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start, it’s like a switch flips and I’m just shoveling food in, thinking, ‘You should stop, you idiot,’ but my hands keep going back to the fridge and I don’t feel like I can make myself stop until everything’s gone or I feel sick.
